header:
Date: 2025-02-17 16:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (NovaGrove - Head of ML Ops), Carlos Ruiz (NovaGrove - VP Eng), Hannah Kim (NovaGrove - Security)
summary: Quick renewal check-in + APAC region onboarding discussion. Customer leaning toward 12-month renewal with a modest capacity bump and APAC seed region. Main blockers: final pricing for APAC Dedicated nodes vs hosted burst, SOC2 evidence and KMS/HSM clarification, and a short latency pilot to validate p95 under 512-token prompts.
topics: Renewal timing and term options (12 vs 24 months)
APAC region onboarding (seed capacity and lead time)
Dedicated vs Hosted for predictable tail latencies and throughput
Security: SOC 2 / KMS / data residency / audit logs
Pilot & benchmark plan (512-token baseline, KV cache behavior)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this tight — 45-ish minutes planned but we have 57 on the calendar so good. Quick intros.
[00:09] Maya Patel: Hi, Maya here. I'm the head of ML ops at NovaGrove.
[00:12] Carlos Ruiz: Carlos, VP Eng.
[00:14] Hannah Kim: Hannah in security.
[00:16] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks. Priya is our systems SE — she'll cover the latency/throughput items.
[00:22] Priya Anand: Hi all. I threw a short agenda in the invite: renewal terms, APAC seed, test plan, and KMS questions.
[00:30] Maya Patel: Yep that's right. We're coming up on contract renewal end of March so want to lock something down in next two weeks. We're planning a small APAC pilot region for Q2, approx 15% of traffic initially.
[00:44] Jordan Lee: Good context. On capacity, are you thinking reserved Dedicated capacity for APAC or just hosted with region add-on?
[00:52] Carlos Ruiz: We need predictable p95 for customer facing flows — some of our endpoints are latency sensitive — so leaning Dedicated but want to understand cost delta.
[01:05] Priya Anand: Understood. Dedicated gives the most predictable tail; hosted with routing and fallback can work but you may see variability under burst. Also we have continuous batching and prefix/KV caching which helps cost, but cache warm-up behavior is important with your distribution.
[01:22] Carlos Ruiz: Quick dumb question — when you say KV cache, is that like a separate redis we manage?
[01:27] Priya Anand: No — sorry confusing wording — it's internal KV cache in the runtime to reuse key/value cache for decoding. It's not external redis; it's a runtime memory cache. (laughs) Apologies.
[01:38] Hannah Kim: On security side: SOC 2 is fine, we need more detail on key management. Can Redwood use our cloud KMS or do you require HSM? We also need audit log retention settings.
[01:50] Jordan Lee: Short answer: we integrate with cloud KMS (GCP KMS, AWS KMS) and can support customer-managed keys; HSM is available as an add-on for private deployments — we'll surface the options in the doc. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM; retention depends on plan but we can provide extended retention as a paid add-on.
[02:06] Maya Patel: Great. Regarding pricing: we're okay with a 12-month if the APAC seed is priced at step-up rather than full Dedicated rate. We don't want to overcommit if APAC performance isn't validated.
[02:18] Jordan Lee: Makes sense; we can do a staged approach: APAC seed as hosted with guaranteed minimum capacity and a conversion path to Dedicated at a prefixed rate. I'll add the exact numbers to the quote.
[02:29] Carlos Ruiz: For the pilot, Priya, what do you need from our side?
[02:33] Priya Anand: Ideally a sample prompt set and traffic profile: tokens per request distribution, p95 service time target, concurrent clients. We'll run a baseline on our side with model X (we'll propose a compatible open model) to show expected p95 and cost per token. Also we want to test cold-start + KV cache warm-up — that tends to affect early tail latencies.
[02:54] Maya Patel: We can share a sanitized prompt set — nothing PHI — and expected QPS. We're about 300 peak QPS now and average tokens per request are 180 but peak flows hit around 480 tokens occasionally.
[03:09] Priya Anand: Perfect. We'll run tests for 512-token targets to cover your peak. We'll include a histogram of latencies and p95 numbers.
[03:18] Hannah Kim: For data residency, APAC seed needs to ensure data doesn't leave region for the pilot. Is that nailed down?
[03:25] Jordan Lee: On our hosted side, routing can keep inference in-region; for strict residency we recommend Private (VPC) or Dedicated in a customer VPC. For a pilot we can ensure region-local routing with audit logs showing egress — we'll include that in the pilot runbook.
[03:40] Carlos Ruiz: Any notable competitor differences we should know about? We evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic earlier — we liked Redwood's rollout controls and clear observability around costs. The gap was around region availability and on-prem options but seems like you're addressing that.
[03:55] Jordan Lee: Appreciate the feedback. We're trying to keep all three modes consistent.
[03:58] Maya Patel: One more commercial question — can we keep a fixed per-token rate for the term if we commit to a 12-month? The variable usages spike and we want some predictability.
[04:08] Jordan Lee: We can offer blended committed rates with overage tiers; for Dedicated it's simpler since it's capacity-based. I'll model both in the quote.
[04:15] Priya Anand: On the technical, one practical note: When you move from hosted to Dedicated, KV cache invalidation patterns can change, so you'll see a brief variance in tail latencies during cutover. We'll recommend a canary/cutover window and pre-warm steps.
[04:33] Carlos Ruiz: That's fine — we can schedule cutover after hours.
[04:36] Hannah Kim: For compliance, we need an explicit SOC 2 report and a description of key encryption in transit and at rest. Also, do you support customer-managed KMS keys in Dedicated?
[04:47] Jordan Lee: Yes, customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we support CMEK with cloud KMS; HSM is an add-on. I'll attach SOC 2 summary and the KMS integration whitepaper.
[04:58] Maya Patel: Awesome. On timeline, if we get the pilot running next week and results look good, we can sign a 12-month amendment by March 10.
[05:05] Jordan Lee: That timeline works. So immediate next steps: Maya share traffic & prompt set (due 2/19), Priya run baseline (due 2/21), Jordan send quote + contract amendment with APAC step-up option (due 2/20), Hannah to confirm KMS/HSM requirements (due 2/18).
[05:20] Carlos Ruiz: One nuance — we have a secondary workload that's sensitive to jitter; what's typical p99 on your Dedicated nodes for 512 tokens?
[05:27] Priya Anand: It depends on model and hardware; on our recommended q4-quant profile p99 for 512 tokens on a dedicated cluster is typically sub-900ms on A100 equivalent, but I'll put exact numbers from the baseline. Keep in mind p99 is noisy; we target p95 for SLOs.
[05:43] Maya Patel: Ok cool. Anything else?
[05:45] Hannah Kim: We'll want the audit log schema and the retention export instructions.
[05:50] Jordan Lee: Noted — we'll include the schema + example in the security packet.
[05:54] Jordan Lee: Alright folks thanks — we'll follow up with the quote and the pilot runbook.
[05:58] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone.
[05:59] Jordan Lee: Bye.
questions: What's the expected lead time for APAC Dedicated provisioning?
Can Redwood sign a BAA? (Customer to confirm)
Do you provide HSM or only cloud KMS for hosted?
